rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / CLASSES / CHAPTER 14

slides.title: Inheritance and composition
slides.main: Inheritance means "is a", composition means "has a": the choice sets how flexible your code is.

items.title: Inheritance
items.sub: The child takes all from the parent

slides.title: Inheritance
slides.main: The "is a" link: a dog is an animal, so inheritance fits.

slides.title: Overriding and super
slides.sub: Replace the behavior or extend it
slides.main: When overriding a method, decide if you need the parent version and call it via super().

slides.title: Polymorphism
slides.main: Add a class and the loop speaks anew with no edits. All it needs is a method with the same name.

slides.title: Method resolution order
slides.main: Multiple inheritance is mostly for mixins; in doubt, use composition.

slides.title: Abstract classes
slides.sub: A contract: subclasses must implement it
slides.main: A template with no objects of its own: until all abstract methods are implemented, no instance can be created.

body.text:
9
TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class Shape without an implementation for abstract method 'area'

slides.title: Composition
slides.main: Prefer composition: swap parts without touching the rest.

slides.title: isinstance and type
slides.main: isinstance honors the hierarchy, type does not; Pythonic is to try, not check.

body.text:
class Animal:
    pass

class Dog(Animal):
    pass

d = Dog()
print(type(d) is Animal, isinstance(d, Animal))
print(hasattr(d, "voice"))

slides.title: Magic methods and subclasses
slides.main: When overriding, keep the meaning: a subclass fits wherever a parent was expected.

slides.title: Mixins
slides.main: A mixin adds a skill without "is a": mix it in and the class gets to_dict.

slides.title: Example: shapes
slides.sub: Common interface on top, implementations below
slides.main: A new shape is one new class; the rest of the code stays.

slides.title: Common mistakes
slides.main: Inheritance is not a way to "reuse code": with no "is a", use composition.

body.text: Also: too-deep hierarchies, a changed signature on override, a diamond without understanding MRO.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: Done with classes: now you describe your own data types.
